svg.title: Temporal policy and governed memory
svg.desc: A mobile-first flow showing canonical Agent Memory producing a versioned governed projection, a compatibility gate checking currentness, schemas, temporal horizon, isolation and actual evaluated context, consumer-specific Dogwood or Cedar-family views, an external policy decision, monotonic composition with PAMA, and returned decision evidence. Schema or currentness changes create new compatibility evidence rather than rewriting history.
svg.text: Temporal policy and governed memory
Memory can evolve. Policy input must prove it still means what the consumer expects.
HARD INVARIANTS
canonical memory != consumer trace
valid JSON != semantic compatibility
temporal match != current authority
policy decision != execution evidence
A deterministic policy engine can still evaluate stale semantics.
01 CANONICAL AGENT MEMORY
Keep the full memory semantics here
identity · provenance · event time · valid/current time
scope / isolation · domain schema · correction / supersession
revocation · deletion · derivation · currentness · PAMA
Agent Memory owns memory meaning and lifecycle.
External policy systems do not become the canonical memory store.
Historical truth and current applicability remain separate.
02 VERSIONED GOVERNED PROJECTION
Export only what the consumer needs
minimal historical events · current context · scope · source refs
projection profile/version · domain-schema identity · digest
The projection is reconstructable derived state.
A rebuild after schema migration receives a new identity.
Consumer vocabulary stays outside canonical memory.
03 COMPATIBILITY + CURRENTNESS GATE
Prove the projection still matches the target contract
source currentness · source/domain schema · projection version
target action/event schema · policy/store identity
required temporal horizon · available temporal horizon
isolation strategy · validated partition evidence
projected context digest · actually evaluated context digest
current · migration_required · incompatible · unknown
Known incompatibility beats migration; migration beats unknown.
Only fully established required evidence becomes current.
unknown != current · compatibility has authority_effect = none
04 CONSUMER-SPECIFIC DERIVED VIEW
Specialized systems keep specialized representations
Dogwood
bounded temporal event trace · event schema · providers · pins
Cedar / Cedarling
typed principal/action/resource/context · policy schema/store
dynamic current context · decision diagnostics / logs
These views are derived and replaceable.
Agent Memory history != Dogwood trace != Cedarling cache
05 EXTERNAL POLICY DECISION
Policy evaluates the compatible view
ALLOW / DENY · determining policies · request/context identity
A temporal match is decision evidence, not memory authority.
Policy ALLOW != human approval != execution
06 MONOTONIC COMPOSITION
External policy may tighten, never silently widen PAMA
PAMA deny + external allow -> deny
PAMA review + external allow -> review
PAMA allow + external deny -> deny
07 RETURNED EVIDENCE + LIFECYCLE LOOP
Decision evidence returns through normal provenance and lifecycle rules.
Schema/currentness change -> new evaluation or rebuild; history stays immutable.
Research: docs/research/temporal-policy-semantic-mediation.md · Decision candidate: ADR-030
